Is there a lay-down area designated for this project? Answer: There are no designated laydown areas on the drawings. AHU-2., Limited space on roof near Temp Unit, and limited space on 10th floor near AHU-2 area. AHU-11, Limited Space on Shaft 5 Roof, and inside near unit. AHU-7 extremely limited space inside Shaft 2, near units. There is nothing on drawings showing any pre-determined areas so contractors should assume no laydown area permitted. Is parking available for contractors on-site? Answer: No. One dumpster or one parking spot. Due to volatile material price fluctuations and unpredictability of the market, will the government agree to pay for Stored Materials on this project to avoid price increases post bid? Documentation of material invoice/packing slips, photo, and insurance backup information for each relevant charge would be provided. Answer: No If a project runs past initial period of performance, can material costs be submitted then? Save it and plot the larger PDF On plan page AS-801-AD there are three openings which state the existing doors are to be removed, stored, cleaned and reinstalled.Â These are units #78-1, 84 and 85.Â That same comment states to provide new hardware.Â May I assume the frames will also be ETR and only price the hardware?Â Please confirm and thank you again. Answer: 2F should be Metal; 2T should be Wood DISREGARD THIS ANSWER Specifically, Door Type 2 appears to correspond to a consistent door elevation (narrow lite vision panel), with the suffix F or T potentially indicating glazing type (fire-rated vs. tempered), rather than door material. The response provided does not adequately define or quantify the required scope of work for bidding purposes under this firm fixed-price contract. Additional information is required to establish an accurate takeoff and pricing, including, but not limited to: piping material type, pipe size, estimated linear footage of repair/replacement, existing drain conditions, required demolition limits, and clarification as to whether the existing drain is to be repaired partiallyÂ or replaced in its entirety. Detailed drawings and/or a clearly defined scope of work should be provided. Answer: From the Solicitation Narrative, The (3) drains for the pass thru Sterilizers and the (1) drain for the existing Cart Washer need to be repaired to stop them from leaking. This includes work on the floor below in the generator room and electrical substation area. Minimum scope of work includes: a. Hand chipping around each drain perimeter b. Cleaning surrounding area c. Resealing existing drain to existing concrete d. Replacing drain piping/fittings that are rotted and leaking e. Replacing drain if it is damaged during repairs Adding the following additional information: f. Contractor to include 10 LF of drain piping , one elbow, one coupling for each drain g. VA will remove all Cart Washer ancillary equipment to expose drain area for repairs Question 5: Drawing set VA+SYRACUSE+SPS++Drawings++4 identifies Fellenzer Engineering LLP as the Engineer of Record; however, the revised/addendum sheets do not appear to bear an engineer s stamp/signature. The previous sheets marked Reference Only Use Addendum Sheet contain the Engineer of Record stamp, but the corresponding replacement sheets in Drawing Set ++4 do not. Please clarify whether the revised/addendum sheets were intentionally issued without an Engineer of Record stamp and confirm that these drawings were reviewed and approved for bidding and construction use. Answer: The VA reserves the right to modify drawings as they see fit. All changes were made prior to this solicitation, and with any drawing that was changed to PE stamp was removed as a result. Additionally, the VA has the right to issue drawings or projects without stamped drawings It is not within the Contractors right to question if the drawings have been reviewed or approved.
